clue.text: Obviously in the clear — terribly obvious in space

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone innocent is plainly visible floating out in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles all fourteen letters of OBVIOUS IN SPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person beyond any doubt or blame is plainly cleared of wrongdoing; the phrase is an idiom for innocence.

clue.text: Beauty holding a cake cut in half or a trifle

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the other pieces inside itself

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: cut in half means only the front half of the cake's name survives

parts.note: a gateau is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: A lovely woman carrying a halved cake, or perhaps a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in half' keeps only the front half of the cake's name. 'trifle' looks like the British layered pudding but means something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is something of little importance, a mere trivial thing.

clue.text: Servant's farewell to leader

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye

indicators.note: leader here means just the opening letter of the little word to

explanation.surface: A servant says goodbye to their master.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a man's personal attendant, a kind of domestic employee.

clue.text: Areas of Kent and Northumberland have a fragrance characteristic of old age

parts.note: Kent lies in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
Northumberland lies in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
a scent is a pleasant smell

explanation.surface: Two English counties share a smell that reminds you of old people.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent and Northumberland are English counties at opposite corners: the far south-east and far north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent means growing old, showing the decline that comes with ageing.

clue.text: Clothing from Asian rails oddly neglected

indicators.note: oddly neglected means the first, third, fifth letters and so on are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Garments taken from an Asian clothes rail, done carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Saris are garments worn by women in South Asia, so they are items of dress.

clue.text: Unreal island girl swallowing a drink

indicators.note: swallowing means the girl's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A girl on an island knocks back a drink and things seem dreamlike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it is not real.

clue.text: Cake decoration is a winter phenomenon

definitions.meaning: the sugary coating spread over a cake
ice forming on surfaces such as aircraft wings or roads in cold weather

explanation.definitionFit: Both the sugar coating on a cake and the build-up of frost on surfaces share the word.

clue.text: Director meets Queen Mary finally in sister's home

parts.note: Trevor Nunn is a well-known British theatre director
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: finally means just the closing letter of Mary is used

explanation.surface: A film director meets Mary, Queen of Scots, at the end in a sister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Trevor Nunn ran the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre. 'sister' is a nun, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is where religious sisters, or nuns, live together.

clue.text: Just graduate going to bank

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A new graduate heads straight to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in 'bank on', not the money building.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means only just, by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Some professional golf star

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A leading player in the professional golf world.
explanation.definitionFit: Algol is a well-known variable star in the constellation Perseus.

clue.text: Recital arranged by people outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for people wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a nation is a people
arr. is the musical abbreviation for arranged

explanation.surface: A concert performance set by people out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recital' looks musical, matching 'arranged', but it means a spoken account.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a telling or account of events, as is a narration.

clue.text: What people leave in cars

definitions.meaning: the property and possessions a person leaves behind on dying
estate cars, the British term for station wagons

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a dead person's assets and long-backed station wagons, which Britons call estate cars.

clue.text: English novel: "On The Beach"?

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An English novel titled On The Beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, matching the real novel title On the Beach, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the pebbles covering many seashores, so it is found by the sea.

clue.text: Returned deposit cheers Black Sea resort

indicators.note: Returned means the word for deposit is turned to read the other way

parts.note: to lay is to deposit or put down, as a hen lays
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A deposit was paid back with thanks at a Black Sea holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a seaside town in Crimea on the Black Sea coast, famed for the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Backer's clean after drug is found

indicators.note: after means the cleaning word is placed following the backer

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a show
to dust is to clean

explanation.surface: A financial backer cleans up once some narcotics are discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel dust is a street name for the drug PCP.

clue.text: Poem written about a midwinter lake with style and grace

indicators.note: about means the poem goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem
the middle two letters of winter

explanation.surface: A poem about a lake in midwinter is written with polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midwinter' gives NT, the middle of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something elegantly means doing it with refinement and poise.

clue.text: Playwright's constant regret about date in Rome

indicators.note: about means the two pieces before it are turned round together

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant
to rue is to regret
the Ides was a date in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: A writer keeps regretting a date in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PI + RUE into EURIP. The Ides of March is the famous Roman date.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was a tragic dramatist of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Majority formerly for a game of cards

definitions.meaning: the age at which one came of age in Britain before 1970

explanation.definitionFit: Coming of age used to be at that age, and the same number names the card game blackjack.

clue.text: Engineer in aircraft or ship

indicators.note: in means the engineer is put inside the aircraft

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An engineer at work in an aeroplane or a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo vessel.

clue.text: Roman goddess in favour of fish

parts.note: for means supporting
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A Roman goddess who backs fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortuna was the Roman deity of luck.

clue.text: Buckle underbear

definitions.meaning: to buckle is to give way under pressure
the paper ran 'under bear' together: to bear is to produce, as a tree bears fruit

explanation.walkthrough: The paper most likely printed 'Buckle under, bear' with the space lost; 'buckle under' and 'bear' are each a sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrendering under pressure and producing a crop are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Benefit includes divine piece of cake

indicators.note: includes means the benefit word holds the other inside

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine or clergyman

explanation.surface: A welfare payment covers some heavenly cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' means something easy, not food; 'divine' is a noun, a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is British slang for an easy task.

clue.text: Make up one's mind to crack again?

definitions.meaning: to solve once more, a puzzle cracked a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Deciding firmly and solving a puzzle a second time both use the word, the latter split as re-solve.

clue.text: Perhaps a teddy bear, somewhat fed up?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A soft toy perhaps seems a little bit glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like gloomy, but means full of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sated means having eaten one's fill, satisfied.

clue.text: Father leaves newer place in Surrey

indicators.note: leaves means the father's abbreviation departs from the word

parts.note: fresher means newer
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A father moves out to a newer home in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a commuter town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in the county of Surrey.

clue.text: In a sort of Piper a considerable number flew

indicators.note: In means the large number goes inside the kind of piper

parts.note: the Pied Piper of Hamelin
a lot is many

explanation.surface: A Piper Cub plane with lots aboard took to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piper' suggests the aircraft maker, matching 'flew', but it is the Pied Piper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot a plane is to fly it, so piloted means flew.

clue.text: US city? Try South African city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a go is a try

explanation.surface: Asking about a US city, then suggesting one in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South African' is split: South gives S and the definition is African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria.

clue.text: Nancy's one batty virgin

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, and un is French for one
touched means slightly mad

explanation.surface: A woman named Nancy is a dotty innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the city in north-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something virgin is pristine, never handled or spoiled.

clue.text: Greek bird making beastly noise

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A Greek bird making an animal sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is a low rumbling sound made by an animal such as a dog.

clue.text: A mystery studio broadcast with this, we hear

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio studio puts out a puzzling programme for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' is not a sound-alike signal here; it is the definition, describing the body's hearing apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ears and associated nerves form the apparatus by which humans perceive sound.
